quest.first-road.title: Somewhere to drive
quest.first-road.text: Right! Nobody has ever moved to a field. Lay some road and we will have somewhere to put the houses beside.
quest.first-zone.title: Room for people
quest.first-zone.text: Beautiful road. Now zone some land beside it — residential, I would say, since we have nobody yet.
quest.first-power.title: Lights on
quest.first-power.text: Houses are wonderfully stubborn about electricity. A plant, and wire to carry it — nobody moves in without both.
quest.first-water.title: Something to drink
quest.first-water.text: And water. I am told people are quite insistent about it. A pump, and pipe close enough to the houses to matter.
quest.first-residents.title: The first neighbours
quest.first-residents.text: Road, power, water, and somewhere to live. That is the whole recipe. Let us see who turns up.
quest.first-jobs.title: Somewhere to work
quest.first-jobs.text: Your neighbours are lovely and entirely unemployed. Zone somewhere for shops or industry and they will have a reason to get up.
quest.first-tax.title: The town's purse
quest.first-tax.text: Everything you build is paid for by the people who live here, at whatever rate you set. Seven in the hundred is where we start. Move the slider either way and watch the monthly figure move with it — that is the whole of the budget, and it is yours.
quest.first-service.title: Somebody has to answer
quest.first-service.text: Houses catch fire and people help themselves to things. A fire station or a police post covers everything within a walk of it — put one where the people are, not where the land is cheap.
quest.first-park.title: Somewhere to sit
quest.first-park.text: A park costs almost nothing and every plot that can see it is worth more. It is the cheapest thing in the catalogue and the closest thing we have to free money.
quest.grow-to-two-hundred.title: A proper little town
quest.grow-to-two-hundred.text: Two hundred residents. That is the point where this stops being a few houses by a road and starts being somewhere. More road, more zoning, and keep the power and the water ahead of the building.
quest.town-of-five-hundred.title: A proper town
quest.town-of-five-hundred.text: Five hundred people. That is a town, not a hamlet. Somebody will want to name a roundabout after you.
quest.industry-or-shops.title: A difference of opinion
quest.industry-or-shops.text: The business association and the industrial foreman have both cornered me this week. They want opposite things and they both want them from you.
quest.industry-or-shops.choice.0: Back the shops. A town centre worth walking to.
quest.industry-or-shops.choice.1: Back industry. Jobs first, prettiness later.
quest.the-high-street.title: The high street
quest.the-high-street.text: You backed the shops, so the shops are your problem now. Let us see a real commercial district.
quest.the-works.title: The works
quest.the-works.text: You backed industry, and the foreman has not stopped smiling. He would like somewhere to put it all.
quest.city-of-two-thousand.title: A city, then
quest.city-of-two-thousand.text: Two thousand residents. I looked it up: that is officially a city in three countries and a large village in one very stubborn one.
quest.keep-the-lights-on.title: Keep the lights on
quest.keep-the-lights-on.text: A city that outgrows its power plant finds out about it all at once. Get well ahead of it.
quest.unclog-the-streets.title: Unclog the streets
quest.unclog-the-streets.text: Your roads are full. Not busy — full. More road, or somewhere nearer for people to work.
quest.city-of-five-thousand.title: Five thousand
quest.city-of-five-thousand.text: Five thousand people. At this size the things you got away with early stop being free — the traffic, the smoke, the districts nobody wants to live in. Fix them and it keeps growing.
quest.the-crime-wave.title: A bad month for locks
quest.the-crime-wave.text: Three break-ins on the same street and the rest of the district has noticed. Crime follows empty pockets and thin policing, and it drags land value down with it. Get it back under control.
quest.after-the-wreckage.title: After the wreckage
quest.after-the-wreckage.text: It is over, and it left a mess. Ruined ground stays ruined until somebody clears it — nothing will build there and nothing will grow there. Take the bulldozer through it and we start again.

stat.noHistory: This city has barely any history yet. The graphs fill in a month at a time.
stat.population.about: How many people live here. Homes fill only where there is power, water and a road.
stat.jobs.about: Places to work, from shops and industry. Fewer jobs than residents and people leave; far more and the shops stand empty.
stat.treasury.about: What the city has in the bank. Income is the tax rate against land value and headcount; upkeep is what you have built.
stat.landValue.about: What the ground is worth, averaged over the city. Parks, water and quiet raise it; pollution and crime lower it.
stat.pollution.about: Dirty air over the developed part of the city. Industry and congested roads make it; parks and distance absorb it.
stat.crime.about: How much goes missing. It follows low land value and thin police cover, and it drags land value down further.
stat.congested.about: Road tiles carrying more traffic than they can hold. Congestion pollutes, and a long commute makes a lot less desirable.
stat.demandR.about: How badly people want to move in. High demand means zone more housing; negative means you have zoned more than anyone wants.
stat.demandC.about: How much commerce wants to open here. It follows residents with money to spend.
stat.demandI.about: How much industry wants to build here. It follows jobs the city cannot yet supply.
stat.verdict.tooSoon: Not enough history to say yet.
stat.verdict.better: Better: {change}% in the right direction over {months} months.
stat.verdict.worse: Worse: {change}% in the wrong direction over {months} months.
